rubric.description: The requested form strings are compact, natural titles, field labels, and buttons. Controls remain identifiable and distinguish registering/reserving a free workshop place from joining a waitlist, which does not reserve a place. The confirmation screen explains the result, so its heading may explicitly confirm registration or neutrally identify that result. Accept valid concise wording alternatives; do not demand a particular heading. Fail for paragraph-length field labels, false status, invented payment operations, or a guarantee that waitlisting reserves a place.

examples.request: The workshop registration form sounds bureaucratic. Clean up docs/form-copy.json using sources/registration.md. These strings are the title, labels, and buttons people see on the form.

files.sources/registration.md:
# Workshop registration

A participant chooses a workshop session and enters their name and email address. The options show date and time. Registration is free. The Save action records a place immediately and sends a confirmation email. If the session is full, the visitor may join a waitlist instead; this does not reserve a place. The confirmation screen explains the result. The form already shows that no payment is due. A clear form label is ordinarily a few words; the app puts policy details in its existing registration guide, not additional help paragraphs on the form.
files.docs/form-copy.json:
{
  "title": "Participant registration facilitation",
  "name_label": "Participant identity designation",
  "email_label": "Electronic correspondence endpoint",
  "session_label": "Session allocation preference",
  "submit_button": "Execute registration finalization",
  "waitlist_button": "Initiate waiting-list enrollment",
  "success_title": "Registration outcome realization"
}
